name: llm_value_protocol_v1
question: Do LLM-formulated hypotheses (roles C1-C3) add value over the deterministic template path?
design: paired, within-source: whenever a formulation call returns a usable LLM hypothesis, the same template family is also rendered with the template's DEFAULT parameters; both variants are scored identically
primary_endpoint: difference in Sharpe (cost model 1x) on ETHUSDT DEVELOPMENT data (last 4 years of the split) between LLM parameters and template defaults. ETH is used because the LLM's context contains BTC development diagnostics only, so BTC development scores would favour the LLM in-sample
secondary: BTC development Sharpe difference (reported, in-context, not decisive)
LLM failure rate (no usable output per call)
share of LLM hypotheses rejected as duplicates or invalid
analysis: after >= 15 pairs: mean paired difference with a 95% bootstrap CI (2000 draws, seed 0) and a sign test

decision_rule.keep_llm_formulation: CI of the primary endpoint lies above 0
decision_rule.disable_llm_formulation: CI includes 0 or lies below 0 AND no secondary endpoint favours the LLM: set army control llm_enabled=false for formulation and reallocate the 3 daily calls to the specialist adversarial/critique roles
decision_rule.inconclusive: otherwise continue to 30 pairs, then apply the same rule without further extension

budget: no additional LLM calls: the experiment piggybacks on the frozen <= 3 calls per cycle
never: the scoring never feeds promotion; validation data and holdouts are not touched
